s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of cerebellar syndrome with increased intracranial pressure
salient_findings: Bilateral blurry vision and morning projectile vomiting
Kinetic and static cerebellar syndrome with ataxia, imbalance, uncoordinated movements, bilateral nystagmus, and stage I bilateral papilledema
Inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis on brain MRI
key_facts: 44-year-old woman
4-month history of severe headaches
Headaches are paroxysmal and aggravated by changes in position
Associated with bilateral blurry vision and morning projectile vomiting
Neurological examination shows cerebellar syndrome
Ataxia, imbalance, uncoordinated movements, bilateral nystagmus, and stage I bilateral papilledema are present
Routine blood tests are unremarkable
Noncontrast CT of the head shows no abnormalities
Brain MRI shows an inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis
Lesion is hypointense on T1-weighted images and heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted images
Lesion exerts mass effect on the medulla and shows no surrounding edema on FLAIR
Magnetic resonance spectroscopy shows an elevated choline peak and reduced N-acetyl aspartate signal

shortlist.label: Medulloblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches cerebellar vermis location and age

shortlist.label: Hemangioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common in cerebellum and matches imaging characteristics

shortlist.label: Pilocytic astrocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Typically found in cerebellum and has similar imaging features

shortlist.label: Ependymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can occur in cerebellum and presents with increased intracranial pressure

shortlist.label: Cerebellar liponeurocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor that matches location and some imaging characteristics

shortlist.label: Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with cerebellar symptoms and has variable imaging appearance

shortlist.label: Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor that can occur in cerebellum and presents with increased intracranial pressure

shortlist.label: Cerebellar primitive neuroectodermal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Rare and aggressive tumor that matches location and some clinical features

raw.rationale: The lesion's characteristics on MRI, such as being hypointense on T1-weighted images and heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted images with heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration, along with the presence of an elevated choline peak and reduced N-acetyl aspartate signal on magnetic resonance spectroscopy, are consistent with a pilocytic astrocytoma, a common cerebellar tumor in young adults that often presents with increased intracranial pressure and cerebellar symptoms due to its location and potential for slow growth.

rejected.label: Medulloblastoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more aggressive clinical course and often has a more homogeneous appearance on imaging

rejected.label: Hemangioblastoma
rejected.why: Usually has a distinct appearance with a cystic component and a mural nodule, and is more commonly associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease

rejected.label: Ependymoma
rejected.why: Often arises from the ependymal lining of the ventricles or central canal and may have a more heterogeneous appearance due to hemorrhage or calcification

rejected.label: Cerebellar liponeurocytoma
rejected.why: A rare tumor that typically contains lipid components visible on MRI, which was not described in this case

rejected.label: Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor
rejected.why: More commonly associated with cortical locations and often has a multinodular appearance with a 'soap bubble' pattern on T2-weighted images

rejected.label: Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor
rejected.why: Typically presents in younger children and has a more aggressive clinical course with a poor prognosis

rejected.label: Cerebellar primitive neuroectodermal tumor
rejected.why: Similar to medulloblastoma in terms of aggressiveness and prognosis, and often has a more diffuse or infiltrative pattern on imaging
